summary.headline: Q1 FY27 DI pipe volumes fell 27% YoY to 1.20 lakh tons; consolidated EBITDA Rs 139 crore at 9.5% margin, guided to 12-13% by Q3-Q4 FY27.
summary.overview: Standalone and consolidated volumes fell sharply on weak domestic DI pipe demand, with export volumes also hit by Middle East tensions. Management reported consolidated EBITDA of Rs 139 crore (9.5% margin) and PAT of Rs 48.4 crore, while standalone PAT was only Rs 5.9 crore. Management pointed to JJM 2.0 sanctions and irrigation/river-linking pipelines for an H2 FY27 recovery, cut FY27 DI volume expectations to about 5.75 lakh tons, and announced diversification into industrial paints, valves and railway rubber components. Consolidated net debt was Rs 876 crore at 30 June 2026, down about Rs 1,100 crore in FY26.

segments.name: DI pipes and CI pipes (standalone core)
segments.commentary: Q1 volume 1.20 lakh tons, down 27% YoY; FY27 volume now guided at about 5.75 lakh tons versus earlier 6.5-7.0 lakh tons. Order book about 3 lakh tons (about five months), roughly 50% from JJM.

segments.name: T.I.S. Service S.p.A. (Italy, acquired)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about EUR 10 million with EBITDA margin about 13-14%. FY27 exit target EUR 42-45 million revenue, 14-15% EBITDA margin, about 8% PAT margin.

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: Valve revenue about Rs 400 crore; Q1 growth stated at 18% on last year's Q1. Target to double in four years; Indian valve facility to start by end of FY27. Exports from Italy plant to shift partly to India.

segments.name: Industrial paints and protective coatings (new)
segments.commentary: Initial investment about Rs 100 crore for 17,000 kilolitres capacity via brownfield expansion in West Bengal; long-term target Rs 800-1,000 crore revenue and Rs 250-300 crore capex over 4-5 years. Commercial production expected from Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Railway rubber components (gasket plant, Andhra Pradesh)
segments.commentary: Board approved entry today; railway registration expected in 4-6 months; some additional equipment under installation, expected in about three months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 DI pipe and CI pipe volume about 5.75 lakh tons (management said close to last year's level), with better revenue and margin per ton.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected at 12-13% in Q3 and Q4 FY27; Q2 FY27 expected to be at least similar to Q1 levels.
Export share expected at 22-25% of total volumes by end FY27.
Growth expected mainly in H2 FY27 as JJM 2.0 disbursements pick up; management said the Rs 70,000 crore JJM outlay may drive a significant uplift in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28.
FY30-FY31 aspiration of consolidated revenue Rs 7,000-8,000 crore at 13-13.5% EBITDA margin.
Dependence on DI pipes to fall from about 85% to about 55% in four to five years.
capex_capacity: Industrial paints: about Rs 100 crore initial investment for 17,000 kilolitres in West Bengal; phased capex Rs 250-300 crore over four to five years.
Valve plant in India to commence operations by end of FY27, first phase in West Bengal; Asian subcontinent expected to contribute 40-45% of valve business in three to four years.
Ferro alloy: second plant planned adjacent to existing unit at brownfield site; capacity increase in ferroalloy business under consideration.
Management said about Rs 200 crore to be spent in West Bengal over the next year; greenfield Odisha site put on hold; about Rs 700 crore of capital available for investment including acquisitions.
Term debt about Rs 340 crore, scheduled to fall to about Rs 230 crore.
demand_pricing: Central JJM allocation Rs 67,670 crore for FY27; about Rs 10,344 crore sanctioned to states year to date versus Rs 1,560 crore released under JJM in the previous year. Management said about Rs 6,000 crore released so far.
Q1 FY27 production about 1.0-1.1 lakh tons versus about 1.8 lakh tons in Q1 FY26, per management.
Management expects about 12-13% of JJM outlay to come to Company (stated for DI industry share), and 5-7% of irrigation project volumes to convert into DI pipes.
Saudi Arabia accounts for about 2-3% of sales; management expects 1-1.5% to be lost, to be diverted to other GCC and African markets.
Export mix: about 60-70% Western markets (Europe, UK), remaining 40% Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia.
Management called current DI realisation levels rock bottom and the worst DI year in India since 1994.
States active under JJM 2.0: Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu; UP and Rajasthan expected to pick up.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the JJM 2.0 sanctioned amount is translating into orders for the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 10,000 crore is sanctioned and about Rs 6,000 crore released, with the balance expected soon. Direct order conversion is hard to establish because sanctions largely reimburse state spend; order booking is expected to pick up substantially in the next month or two.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Saudi Arabia's duties on DI pipe imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi Arabia is about 2-3% of sales; management assumes about 1-1.5% will be lost and diverted to other GCC and African markets. It cited Electrosteel's anti-dumping duty of 17% versus 30% for other Indian manufacturers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 DI pipe volume estimate and export expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 volume now about 5.75 lakh tons versus earlier 6.5-7.0 lakh tons guidance. Export volume so far is about 21,000 tons in Q1, with exports expected at 22-25% of total volumes by year end; mix is 60-70% Western markets and 40% Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia.

qa_highlights.question: Why is volume guidance muted despite the large JJM outlay, and will H2 see a boost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY27 is substantially slower and growth comes in H2, as states had run out of steam in H2 FY26 and restarting takes one to two months. Q1 production was about 1.0-1.1 lakh tons versus 1.8 lakh tons in Q1 FY26. Management agreed a significant boost in Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28 is expected if the Rs 70,000 crore is consumed.

qa_highlights.question: What are DI realisations and is pricing bottoming?
qa_highlights.answer: Net realisation about Rs 55,000/ton in Q1 FY27 versus about Rs 50,500/ton in Q4 FY26, or about Rs 62,000/ton on revenue basis. Management called current levels rock bottom and the worst DI year in India since 1994.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated EBITDA margin about 9.5% in Q1 versus about 6.5% in Q4 FY26. Management guided 12-13% in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and said Q2 will be at least similar to Q1, conservatively.

qa_highlights.question: Industrial paints: capex phasing, timelines and products?
qa_highlights.answer: Initial Rs 100 crore for 17,000 kilolitres via brownfield expansion in West Bengal; capex Rs 250-300 crore over four to five years, with revenue rising from about Rs 250-300 crore in the first two years to Rs 800-1,000 crore. Commercial production expected from Q1 FY28; first phase is in-house with marine applications planned for phase two.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term outlook: FY30-31 revenue, DI dependence and capital deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to consolidated revenue of Rs 7,000-8,000 crore at 13-13.5% EBITDA margin by FY30-31. DI dependence is to fall from about 85% to about 55% in four to five years; about Rs 700 crore of capital is available including acquisitions, and the Odisha greenfield site is on hold.

risks_watch: Pace of JJM 2.0 fund release and order conversion: only about Rs 6,000 crore of Rs 10,344 crore sanctioned is released, and H1 FY27 volumes are guided to be weak.
Margin ramp to 12-13% in Q3-Q4 FY27 depends on cost savings and volume recovery; Q1 consolidated margin was 9.5% and standalone PAT only Rs 5.9 crore.
Export exposure to Middle East tensions and Saudi duties, with about 1-1.5% of sales expected to be lost.
Execution risk on new businesses: industrial paints capex Rs 250-300 crore, valve plant by end FY27, railway gasket registration in 4-6 months, and T.I.S. Service FY27 exit targets.
Working capital debt movements and term debt reduction from about Rs 340 crore to about Rs 230 crore; monitor net debt of Rs 876 crore.
Management did not commit to a buyback when an investor raised it, so capital allocation intent remains unclear.
key_quotes: So, most definitely this is rock bottom.
Going forward, I think Q3 FY'27, Q4FY'27, we should be hitting EBITDA number of 12% to 13%.
Conservatively speaking, we won't do worse than where we are today.
The growth will really come in H2 of FY'27.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term water infrastructure demand and margin recovery, but cautious on near-term volumes, saying H1 FY27 will be slow. It was evasive on order-book conversion from JJM sanctions and on buyback questions, and it gave few hard numbers on Saudi and paint capex phasing.
